item: Auto-switch never fires for long high balls (AIR_AND_LOOSE and AUTO), and this case is untested
detail: The brief says AIR_AND_LOOSE (and AUTO) switches when the ball is airborne or loose and another teammate will clearly reach it first. In /home/user/Fifa/src/sim/control/switching.ts, autoSwitchTick only acts within AUTO_WINDOW = 60 ticks of b.lastTouchTick (line 716). computeEff only looks LOCAL_TUNING.looseHorizonTicks = 120 ticks ahead, and line 726 returns when the best candidate's arrival is over 120 ticks. So if the ball first drops below reachHeight (2.3 m) more than about 180 ticks after the strike, the switch can never fire. That holds during the flight and also after the ball lands and bounces, until someone touches it. I reproduced this with a scratch probe, not committed, that calls switchTick with the module's own drag and bounce model. The opponent strikes from x=20, our defender stands at the landing spot and the controlled player is far upfield. Results: high lob at 22 m/s and 0.95 rad (lands at tick 193), 26 m/s and 0.95 rad (220), and a long goal kick or clearance at 30 m/s and 0.7 rad (198) gave no switch in either AIR_AND_LOOSE or AUTO; the player stayed on slot 9. Shorter flights do switch: 20 to 32 m/s at 0.62 rad, 16 to 20 m/s at 0.95 rad, and 24 m/s at 0.8 rad. The result is that on an opponent's long ball over the defence, the user keeps a far-away player for the whole flight, which is the main case the air-ball setting exists for. Possible fixes: scale the window by the ball's time to become playable, or extend the horizon for airborne balls (or drop the line-726 guard for them). Then add a regression test with a flight of 3 s or more. The existing air-ball tests only cover short flights.
